title: Seamless model swap and KV consistency guide
author: Riley Chen
body:
Summary:
This playbook describes a prescriptive, low-risk procedure for swapping active model variants and migrating KV cache shards without violating session consistency guarantees or significantly degrading tail latency. It combines a verified orchestration recipe, telemetry checks, and rollback criteria suitable for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Scope & audience:
- Audience: runtime engineers, release engineers, SRE on-call, platform integrators.
- Applies to: model binary swaps, kvcache layout migrations, topology changes that rebind session affinity (shard moves, NUMA rebinds).
- Not covered: full cluster reboots, GPU firmware upgrades, application-layer prompt changes.

Goals & success criteria:
- Zero user-visible correctness regressions for in-flight sessions (consistency goal).
- No more than 2x degradation of P95 latency during controlled canaries.
- Automatic, deterministic rollback path on defined error thresholds.

Key definitions and guarantees:
- Strong session consistency: a session's KV prefix and cache must remain readable for the lifetime of a conversation until explicit eviction.
- Live-swap: replacing the active model binary for a shard without terminating incoming connections.
- Drain-and-rebind: moving session ownership by draining new requests from a source shard, replaying KV as needed, and binding to a destination shard.

Architecture overview (concise):
- Orchestration layer (Orch): issues swap commands, coordinates canaries, and sets routing policies.
- Shard controller (SC): enacts bind/unbind, coordinates KV replication, and performs drain.
- KV layer: multi-tiered prefix cache with ephemerality flags and fast-lookup index.
- Frontdoor router: routes requests by session token -> shard map; can be flipped to prefer new shard when canary progresses.

Consistency models and tradeoffs:
- Option A (Strong): Synchronous KV snapshot+handshake with two-phase commit. Guarantees no missing keys at cost of higher latency during swap windows.
- Option B (Eventually consistent): Shadow-replication with read-fallback to source shard. Lower latency, but requires careful time-bounded fallbacks and observability.

Recommended default for production: hybrid approach. Start with Option B during canary periods with strict telemetry; for full rollout switch to Option A for final cutover when load is predictable.

Preflight checklist (automatable):
1) Validate model artifact checksum and signature: sha256sum and k8s image signature present.
2) Confirm destination shard has >= 1.5x memory headroom for KV warmup.
3) SLO budget check: current error budget >= planned swap budget (default 0.5%).
4) Open on-call window and post runbook link to #runtime-ops.
5) Gather baseline telemetry (P50/P95/P99 tokens/latency, error-rates, kv-miss-rate).

Step-by-step migration playbook (operational steps):
1) Prepare canary routing rule:
   - Orch: create canary route rule (1% traffic) mapped to destination shard with "shadow-read: true" and "write-back: false".
   - Confirm no destructive flags set.
2) Warmup and shadow replication (10-30 minutes typical):
   - Trigger KV prefetch: SC issues async prefetch for top-10% hottest prefixes via background task.
   - Monitor kv-warmup-progress: expect >80% hot prefix residency within window.
3) Telemetry gating during canary (continuous):
   - p50/p95 latency delta <= +30% and p99 delta <= +60% vs baseline.
   - kv-miss rate on destination <= 2x baseline.
   - error-rate increase <= 0.2% absolute.
   - No functional anomalies in downstream evals (sampled prompts).
   - If any gate trips, abort canary and rollback to previous routing.
4) Incremental ramp (phased percentages):
   - 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% over multiple verification steps (15-60m between steps).
   - At each step, run automated smoke tests and fuzzed prompt validation against responses to detect semantic drift.
5) Final cutover (atomic rebind):
   - Switch routing map atomically: Orch flips session token assignment and marks source shard for graceful deprecation.
   - If Option A chosen: perform synchronous KV handshake before flipping (blocking window).
   - Wait 3x observed median warmup latency before marking migration complete.
6) Post-cutover validation and tidy-up:
   - Mark source shard as "standby" for 1 hour to serve any read-fallbacks and then evict.
   - Run integrity-check job to confirm no missing session prefixes.
   - Update catalog/version metadata and notify product/clients if required.

Rollback criteria and steps:
- Auto-rollback triggers (any one):
  * sustained p99 latency > 2x baseline for 15m.
  * error-rate spike > 1% absolute for 5m.
  * kv-miss rate on destination > 5x baseline for 10m.
  * semantic-eval failures (failing >3 out of 20 sampled prompts).
- Rollback procedure:
 1) Orch reassigns routing map back to source shard (atomic).
 2) Destination shard switches to read-only and begins cache eviction.
 3) Post-rollback alerting: tag incident and capture traces for triage.

Operational knobs and configuration examples:
- CanaryRoute YAML example:
  ---
  kind: CanaryRoute
  metadata:
    name: model-swap-canary-1
  spec:
    percent: 1
    shadow_read: true
    write_back: false
    metrics_gates:
      - latency_p95_delta_ms: 100
      - kv_miss_rate_ratio: 2.0

- Shard binding config snippet:
  shard_bind_timeout_ms: 30000
  kv_sync_mode: "shadow_async" # options: shadow_async | synchronous_two_phase
  max_prefetch_prefixes: 2000

Observability & required dashboards:
- Canary health panel: p50/p95/p99 latency, ingest QPS, kv-miss-rate, error-rate, session-affinity-violations.
- Integrity panel: orphaned-prefix-count, prefix-staleness-hrs, fallback-read-count.
- Tracing: ensure spans include orch.request_id, shard_id_old, shard_id_new, kv_sync_mode.
- Logs: structured event for steps (canary-start, warmup-complete, cutover-inflight, rollback).

Alerting thresholds (recommended):
- Sev1: p99 > 3x baseline for 10m OR sustained error-rate > 2% for 5m.
- Sev2: p99 > 2x baseline OR kv-miss > 5x baseline for 10m.
- Sev3: p95 > 1.5x baseline OR smoke-test failures during ramp.

Troubleshooting matrix (common symptoms -> checks -> mitigation):
- Symptom: sudden p99 spike after 20% ramp.
  Checks: inspect kv-miss-rate, kernel queue depth, GPU memory pressure.
  Mitigation: pause ramp, reduce percent, initiate partial rollback, increase destination shard headroom.
- Symptom: session-level 500s and missing responses.
  Checks: trace request lifecycle for missing KV reads, check for deserialization errors on new model.
  Mitigation: roll back routing, tag failing model artifact for analysis.
- Symptom: high fallback-read-count from frontdoor.
  Checks: verify prefix ingestion pipeline on destination, examine network egress errors between shards.
  Mitigation: restart prefetch workers, rerun KV replay on subset of prefixes.

Diagnostics commands and snippets:
- Show current canary rules:
  # rctl canary list --namespace prod
- Force a single-session rebind for testing:
  # rctl session rebind --session-id <SID> --to-shard shard-42 --mode dry-run
- Inspect shard health and kv stats:
  # shardctl status shard-42 --format json | jq '.kv_stats | {miss_rate,hot_prefixes,mem_used}'

Postmortem data collection (prescribed):
1) Export span traces for the migration window +/- 15 minutes.
2) Export kv-metrics timeline and compare hot-prefix residency before/after.
3) Snapshot sample requests and responses for semantic regression testing.
4) Correlate scheduler/kernel metrics (GPU occupancy, kernel latency) with tail latency spikes.

Ownership and escalation:
- Primary owner: runtime-serving-team@redwood.com (oncall rotation in #runtime-oncall).
- Secondary owner: infra-sre@redwood.com.
- Escalation path: oncall -> runtime tech lead -> SRE manager -> Eng Director.

Appendix A: example smoke tests (automated):
- Test 1: top-20 prompts from prod anonymized corpus; assert token-level edit distance < 5% vs baseline.
- Test 2: prefix read/write roundtrip: perform 100 session-rewind operations, assert no missing keys.

Appendix B: known-risk checklist before private deployments:
- KMS key ACLs validated for destination host.
- Network egress rules between shards in VPC are permissive for replay channels.
- HSM-backed signing available if two-phase commit is used.
